meta.description: mndict LoRA pilot dataset v1 (2026-09-05). Schema-first: train script renders each entry into the exact LFM2.5 runtime prompt/entry format. Composition: 56 entries - 25 common (multi-sense represented), 8 idioms, 5 phrases, 8 rare-but-real (anti-coward set), 10 nonwords (None).

format_contract.entry: headword line, blank line, 'Part of speech: X', blank, 'Meanings:', blank, one or more 'Meaning N (label):' blocks each with definition line, 'Example:', bullet sentences, blank, 'Synonyms:' bullets 'word - gloss', blank, 'Antonyms:' bullets
format_contract.none_rule: if a word genuinely has no synonyms/antonyms, the section contains the single bullet '* none'

meanings.label: physical
meanings.definition: To move in a circle around a central point or axis.
examples: The Earth revolves around the Sun.
The wheels revolved smoothly as the car moved.

meanings.label: figurative
meanings.definition: To center on or be mainly concerned with something.
examples: The discussion revolved around climate change.
His whole life revolves around work.

meanings.label: opening
meanings.definition: An opening in a wall or roof, fitted with glass, that lets light and air into a building.
examples: She opened the window to let in the breeze.
The window is covered with frost.

meanings.label: opportunity
meanings.definition: A short period of time during which something is possible.
examples: We have a small window to catch the flight.
The launch window opens at dawn.

meanings.label: short-lived
meanings.definition: Lasting for a very short time.
examples: Fame on the internet is often ephemeral.
Cherry blossoms are ephemeral, gone within a week.

meanings.label: doorway
meanings.definition: The strip of wood or stone at the bottom of a doorway.
examples: He paused on the threshold of the old house.
Wipe your feet on the threshold.

meanings.label: limit
meanings.definition: The level or point at which something starts to happen or change.
examples: The pain threshold differs from person to person.
Sales crossed the million-dollar threshold.

antonyms: the far side of an entrance

meanings.label: soft speech
meanings.definition: To say something in a quiet, low voice that is hard to hear.
examples: She murmured an apology and looked away.
The crowd murmured in agreement.

meanings.label: continuous sound
meanings.definition: To make a low, steady, indistinct sound.
examples: A stream murmured through the valley.
The audience murmured before the show began.

meanings.label: small pool
meanings.definition: A small pool of water, especially rainwater, on the ground.
examples: Children jumped in every puddle after the rain.
A puddle formed under the leaking umbrella.

meanings.label: bravery
meanings.definition: The ability to do something that frightens you.
examples: It took courage to speak against the crowd.
She showed great courage during the storm.

meanings.label: spice
meanings.definition: Orange-yellow stigmas of a crocus, used to color and flavor food.
examples: The rice was perfumed with saffron.
Saffron is the most expensive spice in the world.

meanings.label: color
meanings.definition: A deep orange-yellow color.
examples: Monks wore saffron robes.
The sunset turned the sky saffron.

meanings.label: shake with fear or cold
meanings.definition: To shake involuntarily from fear, cold, or weakness.
examples: He trembled at the sound of the bell.
Her hands trembled as she opened the letter.

meanings.label: slight vibration
meanings.definition: To shake slightly, as of a thing.
examples: The bridge trembled under the trucks.
Leaves trembled in the wind.

meanings.label: profession
meanings.definition: A person qualified to treat diseases and conditions of the teeth and gums.
examples: Visit the dentist twice a year.
The dentist filled two cavities.

meanings.label: quick and active
meanings.definition: Fast, energetic, and often businesslike.
examples: They took a brisk walk before dinner.
Trade was brisk all morning.

meanings.label: sharp in manner
meanings.definition: Abrupt or blunt in speech or manner.
examples: Her brisk reply ended the conversation.
The waiter was cheerful but brisk.

meanings.label: gathering of crops
meanings.definition: The process or season of gathering crops.
examples: The wheat harvest begins in September.
A good harvest fed the village all winter.

meanings.label: yield
meanings.definition: The amount of crops gathered.
examples: This year's harvest was double the last.

meanings.label: fast
meanings.definition: Moving or able to move very quickly.
examples: The swift river carried the boat along.
He made a swift exit.

meanings.label: dark shape
meanings.definition: A dark area cast by a body blocking light.
examples: The tree threw a long shadow at sunset.
She sat in the shadow of the wall.

meanings.label: trace
meanings.definition: A small sign or remnant of something.
examples: Without a shadow of doubt, he was innocent.
The old empire lives on only in shadows.

antonyms: the real thing rather than a trace

meanings.label: pardon
meanings.definition: To stop feeling anger toward someone who has wronged you.
examples: She forgave her brother for breaking the vase.
Forgive me for being late.

meanings.label: thankfulness
meanings.definition: The quality of being thankful for kindness received.
examples: He expressed his gratitude with a small gift.
She smiled with quiet gratitude.

meanings.label: disagree
meanings.definition: To exchange angry or strong words in a disagreement.
examples: The couple argued about money again.
They argued over the best route.

meanings.label: give reasons
meanings.definition: To give reasons in support of an idea, often formally.
examples: The lawyer argued that the evidence was weak.
She argued for a smaller budget.

antonyms: admit the other side is right

meanings.label: vehicle
meanings.definition: A two-wheeled vehicle powered by pedals.
examples: He rides a bicycle to work.
My bicycle needs a new tire.

meanings.label: genuine
meanings.definition: Free from pretense; meaning what one says.
examples: Please accept my sincere apologies.
Her smile was warm and sincere.

meanings.label: giving
meanings.definition: Willing to give more of something, such as money or time, than is expected.
examples: A generous donation kept the shelter open.
She is generous with her advice.

meanings.label: larger than usual
meanings.definition: Larger or kinder than usual.
examples: He heaped a generous portion of rice on the plate.
The critics were generous with their praise.

meanings.label: contrast
meanings.definition: Used to introduce a statement that contrasts with what came before.
examples: The plan was bold; however, it failed.
However hard he tried, the knot held fast.

antonyms: introduces a result rather than a contrast

meanings.label: in whatever way
meanings.definition: In whatever way or to whatever degree.
examples: However you look at it, the cost is too high.
Arrange the rooms however you like.

meanings.label: in spite of that
meanings.definition: Used to say that something is true despite what was just said.
examples: The task was hard; nevertheless, she finished it.
It was raining; nevertheless, we went out.

antonyms: marks a conclusion rather than contrast

meanings.label: move fast on foot
meanings.definition: To move quickly using your legs.
examples: He runs five kilometers every morning.
She ran to catch the bus.

meanings.label: operate
meanings.definition: To manage or cause a machine, business, or system to work.
examples: They run a small bakery downtown.
This laptop runs two systems at once.

meanings.label: flow
meanings.definition: To flow or cause to flow.
examples: Rivers run into the sea.
Tears ran down her cheeks.

meanings.label: brightness
meanings.definition: The natural or artificial energy that makes things visible.
examples: Sunlight is the best light for reading.
A single candle gave light to the room.

meanings.label: understanding
meanings.definition: Knowledge or understanding of something.
examples: New evidence shed light on the case.

meanings.label: to die
meanings.definition: An informal, humorous way to say someone or something has died.
examples: The old tractor finally kicked the bucket.
In the film the villain kicks the bucket at the end.

meanings.label: reveal a secret
meanings.definition: To reveal secret information, often accidentally.
examples: Tom spilled the beans about the surprise party.
Don't spill the beans before the announcement.

synonyms: let the cat out of the bag

meanings.label: endure the inevitable
meanings.definition: To force yourself to do something difficult or unpleasant that cannot be avoided.
examples: I finally bit the bullet and visited the dentist.
She bit the bullet and told him the truth.

meanings.label: good luck
meanings.definition: A way of wishing a performer good luck, where saying 'good luck' directly is considered unlucky.
examples: Break a leg in tonight's play!
The director told the cast to break a leg.

meanings.label: slightly ill
meanings.definition: Feeling slightly sick or not as well as usual.
examples: I'm feeling a bit under the weather today.
She stayed home, under the weather with a cold.

meanings.label: very easy
meanings.definition: Something very easy to do.
examples: The exam was a piece of cake.
Fixing the bike is a piece of cake for her.

meanings.label: go to bed
meanings.definition: An informal way to say you are going to sleep.
examples: It's late; I'm hitting the hay.
After the trip he hit the hay at once.

entries.word: cost an arm and a leg

meanings.label: very expensive
meanings.definition: To cost a very large amount of money.
examples: That designer bag cost an arm and a leg.
Repairs on sports cars cost an arm and a leg.

entries.word: let the cat out of the bag

meanings.label: reveal a secret
meanings.definition: To accidentally tell a secret.
examples: Mike let the cat out of the bag about the engagement.
Keep the plan quiet; don't let the cat out of the bag.

meanings.label: very rarely
meanings.definition: Something that happens very rarely.
examples: We see each other once in a blue moon.
Once in a blue moon he cooks dinner.

meanings.label: greeting after absence
meanings.definition: A friendly greeting said to someone you have not seen for a long time.
examples: Long time no see! How have you been?
Well, long time no see, stranger.

entries.word: your guess is as good as mine

meanings.label: I don't know either
meanings.definition: Said to mean that you know no more about something than the person asking.
examples: 'When will the bus arrive?' 'Your guess is as good as mine.'
Why she quit? Your guess is as good as mine.

meanings.label: caution advised
meanings.definition: It is wiser to be careful now than to regret danger later.
examples: Take an umbrella - better safe than sorry.
Double-check the locks; better safe than sorry.

meanings.label: not difficult
meanings.definition: Said to mean that something is not complicated to understand or do.
examples: Just restart the router - it's not rocket science.
Cooking rice is not rocket science.

entries.word: out of sight, out of mind

meanings.label: forgotten when absent
meanings.definition: You stop thinking about people or things that are far away or no longer present.
examples: Once he moved abroad, out of sight, out of mind.
Store the snacks away - out of sight, out of mind.

synonyms: far from eye, far from heart
antonyms: absence makes the heart grow fonder

meanings.label: peddler of books
meanings.definition: A person who travels to sell or distribute books, newspapers, and tracts, especially religious literature.
examples: In the 1800s a colporteur might carry Bibles from village to village.
The society sent colporteurs into the mountains.

meanings.label: whispering sound
meanings.definition: A low, soft, rustling or whispering sound.
examples: A susurrus of leaves filled the quiet street.
The susurrus of the crowd rose and fell.

meanings.label: winter sunshine
meanings.definition: The warmth of the sun in winter.
examples: They stepped outside to enjoy the apricity of the January noon.
Old essays praise the apricity of a clear winter morning.

synonyms: light and warmth of the sun

meanings.label: shoelace tip
meanings.definition: The small plastic or metal tip at the end of a shoelace that keeps it from fraying.
examples: The aglet broke, and the lace frayed at once.
He used tape to replace the missing aglet.

synonyms: a metal cap at a tip

meanings.label: smell of rain
meanings.definition: The pleasant earthy smell that comes after rain falls on dry ground.
examples: Petrichor rose from the pavement as the storm ended.
She opened the window to breathe in the petrichor.

meanings.label: throwing out a window
meanings.definition: The act of throwing someone or something out of a window.
examples: The Defenestration of Prague sparked a thirty-year war.
His sudden defenestration of the printer became office legend.

meanings.label: study of names
meanings.definition: The study of the origin, history, and use of proper names.
examples: Onomastics explains why so many Smiths exist.
She specializes in the onomastics of river names.

meanings.label: false accusation
meanings.definition: A false and damaging statement about someone; slander.
examples: He endured years of calumny from rivals.
The article was pure calumny, as the court found.

meanings.label: smelling of
meanings.definition: Strongly smelling of a particular thing.
examples: The kitchen was redolent of cinnamon and cloves.
Air redolent of pine filled the cabin.

meanings.label: evocative
meanings.definition: Suggesting or bringing back memories or associations.
examples: The song is redolent of old summers.

meanings.label: scornfully mocking
meanings.definition: Mocking in a bitter, grim, or scornful way.
examples: He gave a sardonic laugh at his own misfortune.
Her sardonic remarks cut deeper than anger.
